A cut designed to make contact absence observable

This is a sufficient geometric test. Projection overlap can reject an actually separated interface, which is conservative. A positive separating corridor can exclude contact only if the observation covers all possible connecting material, including the edges, sidewalls, keys, guides and any foreign bridge.

Consequently, the proposed interface has:

Open forks rather than a surrounding sleeve that can touch outside the observed slit.
Relieved bearing lands with finite, calculated optical depth.
Large side clearances around the pin ends and central stem.
No cable, charging contact, actuator guide or transport key permitted to cross the selected open cut.
A complete-profile decision, rather than a gap reading at one central point.

This does not turn an ordinary camera into a certified contact detector. Optical resolution, contamination, installed alignment, thermal movement and unobserved bridges remain explicit conditions.

An independent keeper makes the second release usable

Each temporary leg has two serial release/catch stages, 
𝐴
A and 
𝐵
B. The intermediate body must remain attached to a known side.

State	Stage A	Stage B	Intermediate body belongs to
Carrying the maintenance load	Closed and retained	Closed and retained	Both through the load path
Normal provisional isolation	Open and observed	Positively closed	B side
A persistently or partly jammed	Independent keeper bridges A at its actual position	Then opened and observed	A side through the keeper
Keeper or both routes unavailable	No acceptance; retain support	No acceptance	Defined by the remaining retained hardware

The keeper has its own drive, shoulders and engagement witnesses. It is not an instruction to reverse the jammed A actuator. It captures the failed stage where it is, including a partly open position.
